task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice is posted twice (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount of one copy's posting
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, and the payment's 2900 row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value).
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra IDs are ignored.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

policy.local_time_rule: Company-local time of an instant = the instant plus the UTC offset in force at that instant, taken from utc_offset_schedule (each entry applies from its from_utc instant until the next entry). reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting's ledger timestamp equals its document's timestamp.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances, or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when they share timestamp.
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor, issued_at and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same supplier, date and amount.

task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice is posted twice (see policy.duplicate_rule).

duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value).
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, and the payment's 2900 row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value).
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting's ledger timestamp equals its document's timestamp.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances, or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
posting_rules.opening: One opening journal per open invoice (keyed by invoice_id) and one bank opening journal without IDs, all dated at period start.

policy.journal_grouping: Ledger rows form one journal when they share payment_id; otherwise when they share invoice_id; otherwise when they share timestamp.
policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor, issued_at and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same supplier, date and amount.

policy.duplicate_rule: Two invoices are duplicates when kind, entity_id, currency, total_minor, issued_at and every line item (description, quantity, unit_price_minor, amount_minor, ref) are identical. Invoices that differ in any line ref are separate supplies, even with the same supplier, date and amount.
policy.nulls: Missing references are explicit nulls: an empty field in CSV, null in JSON. Links are never guessed.

task.objective: Audit the reporting period's ledger against the source documents and the policy. Report every discrepancy of the four finding types with evidence, then call submit exactly once. Some ledgers are clean: an empty findings list is the correct answer when nothing is wrong.

duplicate_invoice.meaning: The same invoice is posted twice (see policy.duplicate_rule).
duplicate_invoice.amount: base amount of one copy's posting
duplicate_invoice.evidence: both invoice documents plus, for both copies, the posting row on the same side (both payable/receivable rows, or both expense/revenue rows)

unallocated_payment.meaning: A receipt references an invoice whose open balance covers it, yet part or all of it is credited to 2900 instead of relieving the invoice.
unallocated_payment.evidence: the payment document, the invoice document, and the payment's 2900 row

wrong_fx_rate.meaning: A foreign-currency document is converted with a rate other than the policy rate (wrong date or wrong value).
wrong_fx_rate.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_fx_rate.amount: absolute difference between the posted base amount and the policy base amount, measured on the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_fx_rate.evidence: the document, the posting row (invoices: either side; payments: bank row), and the fx record of the correct date

wrong_period.meaning: A document is posted outside the period its own timestamp belongs to, in company time; only crossings into or out of the reporting period count.
wrong_period.affected_ids: invoice_id or payment_id of the document
wrong_period.amount: posted base amount of the receivable/payable row (invoices) or the bank row (payments)
wrong_period.evidence: the document and one of its posting rows (invoices: either side; payments: the bank row)

conventions.amounts: claimed_amount_minor is a non-negative integer in minor units of the base currency; currency is the base currency code
conventions.ids: affected_ids and evidence_ids are compared as sets after trimming spaces (case-sensitive). A document may be cited by doc_id or by its invoice_id/payment_id. FX records are cited as 'YYYY-MM-DD:SRC:TGT'. A finding needs at least one complete evidence set; extra IDs are ignored.
conventions.matching: one-to-one with the answer key; repeated or unmatched findings are false positives

reward.inspection_steps: every step except the final submit

policy.local_time_rule: Company-local time of an instant = the instant plus the UTC offset in force at that instant, taken from utc_offset_schedule (each entry applies from its from_utc instant until the next entry). Local calendar dates are always taken in company time, whatever offset a timestamp happens to be written with.

reporting_period.rule: A document belongs to the reporting period when start <= its own timestamp < end, compared as instants (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). A posting belongs to the period of its ledger timestamp. A posting must fall in the same period as its document.

ledger_extract.rule: ledger.csv covers the reporting period plus a 7-day cut-off window after it. Items open at period start are carried in by opening journals dated at period start against account 3900.

fx.date_rule: Use the rate dated on the document's local calendar date (issued_at for invoices, timestamp for payments). If no rate is published on that date, use the latest earlier published date.
fx.other_pairs: Rows for pairs other than document currency -> base currency are not used for postings.

posting_rules.posting_timestamp: A posting's ledger timestamp equals its document's timestamp.
posting_rules.sales_invoice: Dr 1100 / Cr 4000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.purchase_invoice: Dr 5000 / Cr 2000 for the base amount of total_minor.
posting_rules.receipt: Dr 1000 for the base amount at the payment-date rate. Allocate the payment to invoice_refs in the listed order, each up to its open balance in document currency. Relieve 1100 at the booked carrying amount: proportional to the allocated share of the open document amount, and the allocation that closes an item relieves its whole remaining carrying amount. Any remainder beyond the referenced open balances, or the whole receipt when invoice_refs is null, is credited to 2900 at the payment-date rate. The balancing difference is posted to 7900.
posting_rules.disbursement: Dr 2000 at the carrying amount relieved, Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.refund: A refund references the invoice whose overpayment it returns. Dr 2900 at the carrying amount of that overpayment credit (proportional if partly refunded), Cr 1000 at the payment-date rate, difference to 7900.
posting_rules.payment_currency: A payment is in the currency of every invoice it references.
